column1: # ZAP baseline rule actions for scripts/zap-baseline.sh.
# Columns are tab separated: rule id, IGNORE|WARN|FAIL, (reason).
# Rules not listed use ZAP's default (WARN).
# KNOWN FINDING (do not "fix" by editing this file): the shipped production stack sends
# Strict-Transport-Security and X-Frame-Options TWICE, once from the outer nginx
# (nginx/site.conf.template server block) and once from the frontend nginx behind it
# (frontend/nginx.conf), because no proxy_hide_header is set. ZAP reports that as
# X-Frame-Options entries). Both rules are WARN until a separate change removes the
# duplicate; then set them back to FAIL. This file keys on plugin ids; whether ZAP's
# config accepts the "-3" / "-2" alert-ref suffixes is UNVERIFIED, so they are not used.
# The baseline is unauthenticated, so the cookie rules (10010, 10011, 10054) only fire if
# the crawl is handed a Set-Cookie; they do not prove the login cookies are safe.

column3: (duplicate X-Frame-Options headers from two nginx layers until fixed; back to FAIL once the outer location hides the inner header)
(X-Content-Type-Options: nginx sets nosniff on every response)
(duplicate Strict-Transport-Security headers from two nginx layers until fixed; back to FAIL once the outer location hides the inner header)
(Server version leak: nginx runs with server_tokens off)
(X-Powered-By leak: no component should emit it)
(cookie without HttpOnly: csrf_token is script-readable by design and ZAP cannot know that, so a crawl that sees it raises this; an unauthenticated crawl sets no cookies at all)
(cookie without Secure on https; only fires once a crawl sees a cookie)
(cookie without SameSite; only fires once a crawl sees a cookie)
(the nginx CSP header still carries 'unsafe-inline' for script and style (the built meta CSP uses hashes); tracked, not yet removable)
(suspicious comments in bundled JS are third-party library text; review new hits)
(Modern Web Application: informational note that the target is a SPA)
(timestamp disclosure: epoch-like numbers in static bundles and API error bodies are not sensitive)
